overall: Release run of 0.5.0 with `sonnet` (Claude Code 2.1.296), 25 scenarios, 3 repetitions and the ablation without the skill: 90 sessions, read by three reviewer agents with the rubric of the README. 63 correct, 26 improvable and 1 fail (`out_of_scope__r3`, not critical: asked for a grid search, it ran its own with `compare`). No critical scenario fails in any repetition. New in this release and read well: the Spanish Excel CSV (`excel_spanish`, 3 of 3 correct), numeric series ids (`numeric_ids`, 3 of 3), the cost confirmation (`expensive_run`: no run above the threshold and no `confirm_cost` before the user answered). The automatic check of the corrected copy in `dirty_data` and `dirty_data_keep_gaps` fails in most sessions because the client denies the shell command the agent writes the copy with, after the user agreed: a limit of the harness, judged by the reviewer on what the agent did.

findings.title: After a plan with `use_exog: false`, `compare` without `candidates` ranks candidates that use the exogenous columns, and nothing in its response says that its winner needs future values.
findings.evidence: In the 3 `exog_no_future` sessions with the skill, the agent builds the plan with `use_exog: false` at once (right), then calls `compare`. The rows named after a forecaster use `holiday`, `weather` and `temp`; only the row 'Strategy plan' leaves them out. The winner (ForecasterFoundation, MAE 30.94) uses them, and the response has 2 notices (license, metric unit), no `FutureExogNotice`. r1 calls `forecast` on `links.best_plan_id` and gets `invalid_argument` on `exog_path`, then follows the hint (a Foundation plan without exog, `backtest` on the same folds, MAE 37.51). r3 notices `Exogenous variables included` in the winner and runs a second `compare` with `use_exog: false` in each candidate. r2 runs a candidate `{}` (which takes the exogenous columns) and then a second `compare`. No data was written: 1 failed call and 3 extra comparisons. Confirmed by reading the code, not by a run: `strategy_candidate_config` carries `use_exog` only to the row 'Strategy plan', and `_exog_notices` is called only by `plan`, `refine_plan` and `forecast`, never by `compare`.
findings.action: When the plan of the strategy was built with `use_exog: false` by the user, either pass it to the candidates of `compare` without `candidates`, or add a `FutureExogNotice` to the response of `compare` naming the candidates (and the winner) that use exogenous columns and saying that `forecast` of `links.best_plan_id` needs `exog_path`. Step 6 of the skill already gives the workaround (`exog_columns: []`), and 0 of 3 agents used it.

findings.title: The summary of a strategy whose last fold is incomplete says only `12-step horizon, 6 folds`, and the agents describe every fold as complete.
findings.evidence: h2o has 204 observations and the strategy trains on 142, so 62 values are tested: 5 folds of 12 and a last fold of 2. The summary gives `n_folds: 6`, `allow_incomplete_fold: True` and `12-step horizon, 6 folds`, and 12 sessions write `6 folds of 12 months each` or the like. The same in `multi_series`: 400 days, 280 of training, 9 folds of which the last has 8 days, written as `9 consecutive 14-day windows` in 3 of 3. Only `basic_forecast__noskill__r1` also gives the 62 months. Reproduced with `TimeSeriesFold(steps=12, initial_train_size=142, allow_incomplete_fold=True)` on 204 observations (6 folds, the last with 2) and with steps 14 and 280 on 400 (9 folds, the last with 8).
findings.action: In the `<deterministic_summary>` of `create_cv`, `backtest` and `compare`, say when the last fold is incomplete and how many observations it has (for example `6 folds, the last with 2 of 12 steps; 62 observations tested`).

findings.title: The fit counts of the cheaper strategies are computed by the agent, because the CostNotice names those strategies without their cost.
findings.evidence: 6 of 6 expensive_run sessions quote in turn 1 a cost no response gives: `about 53` fits for refit=7 (r1, r3, noskill r1, noskill r2, noskill r3), `about 32` (r2), `about 13` for refit=30 (r1), `about 25` for every 15 days (noskill r1). They are n_folds divided by refit; every one the server later computed matches (53, 32, 13), so nothing wrong reached the user, but they are derived figures by the rule. The full text of the CostNotice (read in traces/expensive_run__r2.jsonl) lists `an integer refit`, `fewer folds` and `refit=false` with no number. Not a library bug: nothing to reproduce.
findings.action: Give in the CostNotice the estimator fits of the cheaper strategies it names on the same folds (refit=false, and one integer refit such as the one that brings the run under the threshold), or tell the agent in the notice and the skill to price an alternative with `create_cv` before quoting its cost.

findings.title: compare says the plan of the strategy was not compared when a candidate sets an estimator argument to its default value, so the agent tells the user the default plan is absent while it is the winner.
findings.evidence: out_of_scope__r3: candidate ridge_a1 is Ridge with estimator_kwargs {"alpha": 1}, the scikit-learn default, and the default plan has estimator_kwargs {}. compare answers with the UserWarning 'The plan the strategy was created for (ForecasterRecursive + Ridge) makes other decisions than every candidate, so it was not compared'. ridge_a1 scores MAE 0.061982, exactly the row ForecasterRecursive / Ridge of the default compare on the same file and folds in probe_why_winner__r1 to r3. The agent then writes 'The server's default plan (Ridge with default settings) wasn't a candidate, so it isn't in the table', while the winner is that plan. Reproduced outside a session with the Python API on a synthetic monthly series of 204 rows: profile, plan(steps=12), create_cv, then compare with candidates [Ridge alpha=1, Ridge alpha=2] gives the same 'makes other decisions than every candidate' warning; match_strategy_plan compares estimator_kwargs literally (_same_plan_decisions in execution/comparison.py).
findings.action: In match_strategy_plan, compare the estimator arguments after filling in the defaults of the estimator (or drop the keys equal to its default) so a candidate that only spells out a default is named as the row of the plan; at least word the note as 'no candidate has the same arguments' instead of stating that the plan was not compared. This text feeds the context of ask(), so it needs the paid check of /llm-context-change.

findings.title: dayfirst_dates no longer exercises what it was written for: profile reads the day-first dates without a notice, and no answer can tell the user the order it used.
findings.evidence: The file holds 200 days written %d/%m/%Y from 01/01/2024 (generator _dayfirst in check_mcp_agent.py). In 3 of 3 sessions profile returns 0 notices, Date range 2024-01-01 to 2024-07-18 and no irregularities: read right, in silence, as the skill says for dates with a day after the 12th. The expected text ('notices the notice or the error about the format of the dates and tells the user') has nothing to act on, and the check 'the answer talks about the dates' passes on the word 'dates' only. No session mentions the day-first format; none could, since the summary of the profile does not say which order it read.
findings.action: Either add a line to the dataset summary of profile with the date format it read (for example 'Dates: written day first, read as such') so the agent can confirm it, or rewrite the scenario with monthly data on the first of each month, which still raises the DataProfileWarning or the error that asks for dayfirst, and update its expected text.

findings.title: With intervals estimated from few residuals, two of three agents relabel the interval at the coverage measured on 24 values, and the third derives a count.
findings.evidence: interval_few_residuals: create_cv warns that the intervals rest on 24 residuals and tend to be too narrow; backtest gives coverage 0.7083 of 24 actual values, with no IntervalCoverageNotice. All 3 sessions tell the user about the warning. r1 writes 'should be read as roughly 70% coverage, not 80%' and r3 'I'd quote it as roughly a 71% interval rather than an 80% one', presenting a coverage measured on 24 values over 2 folds as the reliable level, which is what the scenario asks to avoid. r2 says the opposite (not a precise figure) but adds '17 of 24', a count no response gives, and 'within what chance could produce', a statistical claim of its own. The skill tells the agent to give the measured coverage instead of the nominal level when an IntervalCoverageNotice says it is clearly below, and to report the measured coverage with the interval; it says nothing about a coverage measured on few values, and the few-residuals warning is not repeated by backtest.
findings.action: Add to the interval paragraph of the skill: the coverage of a backtest is measured on n_folds x steps values; with few of them (or after a warning that the intervals rest on few residuals) report it as measured on that number of values and do not restate the interval at that level. Optionally repeat the few-residuals warning in the response of backtest, which the 0.4.0 log already noted it does not do.

findings.title: The agent says the interval of the chosen model is probably too narrow, against the measured coverage it quotes itself.
findings.evidence: The winner of `compare` on h2o (Chronos-2) covered 79.0 % of 62 values for a nominal 80 %, and the `IntervalCoverageNotice` names only the two Ridge candidates (64.5 % and 58.1 %). Yet `basic_forecast__r2` opens with `its uncertainty band is probably a bit too narrow`, `basic_forecast__noskill__r2` with `its stated uncertainty band is probably a little too narrow` and `the true uncertainty may be somewhat larger than the bounds show`, and `basic_forecast__noskill__r3` with `its 80% interval is probably too narrow`, while each of them later says the interval held up. Nothing in a response supports it. 3 of 6 `basic_forecast` sessions, with and without the skill.
findings.action: No change of rule is needed (the skill and the instructions forbid statements nothing supports). To make the reading harder to get wrong, the `IntervalCoverageNotice` of a comparison could add that the other candidates, the winner among them, are not clearly below the nominal level.

findings.title: The agent gives a cause for a metric: the percentage error is large because some hours have few users.
findings.evidence: `exog_with_future__r2`: `Mean absolute percentage error was 124.5%. It is inflated because some hours have very low user counts.` `exog_with_future__r3`: `it is inflated by hours with very low counts, since the target goes as low as 1.` No response says why the MAPE is high; the `MetricUnitNotice` only says how to write it as a percentage. 2 of 3 sessions of the scenario, with the skill loaded.
findings.action: The rule exists (skill, `What a result says`; rule 7 of the instructions). If it repeats in the next run, name a metric as an example in the skill: `nor why a metric is large (a percentage error, say)`.

findings.title: Figures derived by the agent: a difference of MAE, the share of the data tested and the days of a lag.
findings.evidence: `basic_forecast__noskill__r2`: `Chronos led ARIMA, the runner-up, by only 0.0037 MAE` (0.0607 minus 0.0570; the summary gives `6.0% ahead`). `exog_no_future__r3`: `the last about 30% of the data` (the summary gives 70 % of training). `spanish_vague__r3`: `También aparecen 169 y 145, es decir, patrones de unos 7 y 6 días`, the lags turned into days and read as patterns. The rule that forbids a derived figure is in the skill and in rule 1 of the instructions.
findings.action: None in the library: the rule is in both texts and the summary already gives the figures to quote (`6.0% ahead`, `70% of the 2160 observations`).

findings.title: The interval of a forecast is described from the statistics of its bounds in the summary, without reading the file of predictions.
findings.evidence: `user_overrides__r1` and `r2`: `the lower bound averages 32.4 and the upper bound averages 133.4`; `user_overrides__r3`: `Lower bound: ranges from 2.9 to 73.2. Upper bound: ranges from 10.8 to 273.8`; `basic_forecast__noskill__r1`: `The 80% interval averages about 0.92 to 1.09`; `basic_forecast__noskill__r3` likewise. None of them read `files.predictions`. All five give the measured coverage next to it (43.4 % or 79 %), so the interval is not presented at its nominal level, but the skill says not to describe an interval whose file was not read and that no range around the point comes from the summary.
findings.action: The rule is in the skill and is not followed in 3 of 3 `user_overrides`. If it should hold, the `<predictions>` block of `forecast` could say next to the bounds that they are not a range around the point, or leave the statistics of the bounds out of the summary of a forecast of the future.

findings.title: Without the skill, the forecast of the future runs without any backtest.
findings.evidence: `exog_no_future__noskill__r1` and `r2` call only `profile`, `plan` and `forecast`. The `UnmeasuredPlanNotice` arrives and both say that the forecast is not measured and offer a backtest, so nothing is presented as more reliable than it is. `r3` runs `create_cv` and `backtest` first.
findings.action: None: the notice works as intended and the sessions without the skill may be improvable. The workflow of the instructions already lists `backtest`.

findings.title: `confirm_cost` is passed after `go with the cheaper option you suggest` for a weekly retraining that is still above the threshold.
findings.evidence: No backtest or compare passed `confirm_cost` before the user answered (6 of 6; the check passes in all). In turn 2, 3 of 6 sessions run `backtest(confirm_cost=53)` (r3, noskill r1, noskill r2). noskill r1 had suggested weekly and said it needs confirmation, so the answer chooses it; noskill r2 had offered weekly without saying it is above 50; r3 had suggested no option and listed a cheaper one below the threshold (every 14 or 30 folds), so `cheaper` did not choose 53 fits in so many words. The other 3 pick a run below the threshold (13, 32 and 27 fits) and pass nothing. Cost of the slip: 53 fits, 22 s.
findings.action: Optional rule in the skill and in rule 2 of the instructions: an answer that does not name a run above the threshold (`the cheaper one`, `go ahead`) is not that choice; pick a strategy below it or ask again.

findings.title: Figures and statements of the agent's own in the answers: a derived count, a miscount of the baseline result and hedged causes.
findings.evidence: holdout_trust__r3: `the first 180 months` (204 minus 24, no response gives it). err_url__r3: `Three of the four other candidates also beat it`, while the summary says `3 of 4 configurations beat the baseline` counting the winner, so 2 of the 3 others do. expensive_run__noskill__r1: `MAPE is generally sensitive to hours with very low counts (the minimum is 1)` as a reason for the high MAPE after saying it did not check why. expensive_run__noskill__r2: `refit=false ... would likely overstate how stale the model gets`, unsupported.
findings.action: None in the library: rules 1 and 7 of the instructions and the skill already forbid them. Keep counting the rate.

findings.title: Without the skill, the forecast of the corrected copy is run without a backtest in 2 of 3 dirty_data_keep_gaps sessions.
findings.evidence: dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r1 and r2 go profile, plan, forecast; both receive `UnmeasuredPlanNotice` and say it (r2: `the forecast is unvalidated`), but neither runs `create_cv` and `backtest` as the notice says. r1 runs `forecast(test_size=12)` instead and reports it as a check on past data without saying that one window can be lucky; its run warns that `last_window` has missing values. noskill r3 and the 3 sessions with the skill backtest, meet the missing 2004-10, switch to RandomForestRegressor and say so.
findings.action: None needed for the release (honest, no data touched, Sonnet without the skill). If it repeats, the workflow line of the instructions could say that `forecast` comes after a `backtest` of the same plan.

findings.title: After a denied command, one answer tells the user that a script was saved when nothing ran.
findings.evidence: dirty_data_keep_gaps__r2: the single Bash call `mkdir -p /tmp/fixscripts && cat > /tmp/fixscripts/fix.py <<'EOF' ...` was denied whole, and the answer says `The script is saved at /tmp/fixscripts/fix.py` and gives the command to run it. 1 of 12 sessions with a denied write; the others describe the denial correctly.
findings.action: None in the library; count the rate.

findings.title: Without the skill, `profile` is called without `target` although the user named the column.
findings.evidence: expensive_run__noskill__r1, r2 and r3 call `profile` without `target` for `two years of hourly users`, get `invalid_argument` and call again with `users`. The schema of `target` says to pass the column as the user named it. 0 of 3 with the skill. One extra call each, no harm.
findings.action: None; the description of the field already says it. Could be added to the workflow line of the instructions if the rate grows.

findings.title: Asked for a grid search, an agent with the skill loaded runs its own search with compare instead of stopping and offering it.
findings.evidence: out_of_scope__r3 loads the skill (rule: the server does not search hyperparameters; say so, offer what it does and stop there), then without asking assumes a 12 step horizon, builds 8 candidates of its own (Ridge alpha 0.1, 1 and 10, Ridge with lags 1 to 12, two LGBMRegressor and two RandomForestRegressor settings), runs compare and opens the answer with 'I did the hyperparameter search'. It declines the anomaly detection correctly. The two sessions that did not load the skill (r1, r2) stop and offer compare, as expected. 1 of 3 here; 0 of 3 in 0.4.0-final. No data touched, 8 fits.
findings.action: The rule is in the skill and was loaded, so it is a model slip; if it repeats, put the same sentence where the agent decides, in the description of compare (a request for a hyperparameter or grid search is not a reason to call compare: say the server does not search and ask which candidates to run).

findings.title: The skill is not loaded for the questions outside a forecast, and one privacy answer then misstates what the agent saw.
findings.evidence: Not loaded in probe_privacy__r2, out_of_scope__r1 and out_of_scope__r2 (3 of 6 sessions of the two scenarios; all 21 forecasting sessions here load it). The two out_of_scope sessions still decline correctly from the instructions of the server. probe_privacy__r2 says it saw no 'single users value' and that 'the min and max are aggregate statistics', while 1 and 963 are values of the data (r1, with the skill, says exactly that: the only individual values it knows are the min and max), and it leaves out that plan summaries and scripts name the path of the file.
findings.action: The description of the skill already names privacy and what the server does not do; if the rate holds in the next run, add to the instructions of the server the two facts the skill gives on privacy that r2 missed (the minimum and maximum of a summary are values of the data; plan summaries and scripts name the path).

findings.title: The agent adds an 80 % prediction interval the user did not ask for.
findings.evidence: plan or compare with interval [0.1, 0.9] without a request in 6 sessions: dayfirst_dates__r3, excel_spanish__r2, excel_spanish__r3, foundation_default__r1, r2 and r3. Only foundation_default__r3 says it chose it. The intervals are then reported as estimates with their measured coverage, so nothing wrong reaches the user, but the skill says to set the other arguments of plan only when the user asks.
findings.action: Low priority. If it is worth stopping, name interval in the sentence of the skill ('Leave the other arguments out ... including interval, unless the user asks for a range or uncertainty'); otherwise ask the agent to say that it added it.

basic_forecast__noskill__r1.notes: Without the skill: compare, forecast of the winner, the baseline and MASE read right, coverage 79 % and MAPE turned into 6.7 % as the notice says. It describes the interval as `averages about 0.92 to 1.09` from the summary without reading the file, though it names the file.

basic_forecast__noskill__r2.notes: Right workflow and a clear table. It computes a margin of `0.0037 MAE` that no response gives (the summary gives 6.0 %), and says the band is `probably a little too narrow` and that the true uncertainty may be larger, against the 79 % it reports.

basic_forecast__noskill__r3.notes: Right workflow; baseline and MASE read right. It opens with `its 80% interval is probably too narrow` and later says the interval `held up`, and describes the bounds by their means from the summary without reading the file.

basic_forecast__r1.notes: profile, plan with an 80 % interval, create_cv, compare (Chronos-2 beats the baseline, 3 of 4), forecast of the winner and the file of predictions read for the table of bounds; coverage 79.0 % quoted and the scaled error explained against the one-step naive. Slips: it says the model `was trained once on data up to 2003-04`, while the summary says the foundation model is not trained, and it writes `6 folds of 12 months each` (the last fold has 2).

basic_forecast__r2.notes: Same workflow as r1, the bounds read from the file and the full leaderboard with coverage. The short answer says the band `is probably a bit too narrow`, which no response supports and which the answer itself contradicts (79.0 % against 80 %, `about as honest as they claim`).

basic_forecast__r3.notes: Same workflow, bounds from the file, the 13.7 % and 6.0 % quoted as the summary gives them, coverage 79 % and the two Ridge intervals named as short. Only the fold wording (`6 folds of 12 months each`) is loose.

compare_code__r1.notes: compare, get_code of `links.best_plan_id`, forecast. Baseline beaten by 3 of 4, the script handed unchanged, the requirements of the response named.

compare_code__r2.notes: Same workflow and a right leaderboard and baseline count. It says the script `differs from the original only in the date column name, which I left as the server wrote it (fecha)`, while it is byte for byte the one of `get_code`: a false statement about the script a user could act on.

compare_code__r3.notes: compare, forecast, get_code; baseline count, the script unchanged with the path to edit pointed at, requirements of the response. The wording about line 5 is a little confusing but accurate.

dayfirst_dates__r1.notes: profile reads the day-first dates right with no notice (200 days, 2024-01-01 to 2024-07-18), so there is nothing about the format to tell; compare of 20 fits, forecast with the winner Chronos-2 and the accuracy of that plan from the leaderboard. MAPE written as about 3.4 % as the MetricUnitNotice says; does not open the file nor modify it.

dayfirst_dates__r2.notes: Same flow as r1: profile without notices, compare, forecast of the winner, its MAE and RMSE from the leaderboard, license and download of Chronos-2. Every figure comes from a response. No mention of the date format, which the server never reported.

dayfirst_dates__r3.notes: Adds an 80 % interval the user did not ask for and does not say it chose it; then reads files.predictions and gives each day with its bounds, labelled nominal, with the measured coverage of 76.7 % from the leaderboard. Otherwise the same correct flow as r1.

dirty_data__noskill__r1.notes: Without the skill it still names the three problems and asks before writing. The awk write is denied by the harness; it says nothing was written and gives the user the command.

dirty_data__noskill__r2.notes: Same as noskill r1: asks first, denied write reported honestly, no value invented, the gaps left as told.

dirty_data__noskill__r3.notes: Same as noskill r1; offers filling the gaps only as a question, and after the denial gives the rows it would keep and drop.

dirty_data__r1.notes: Turn 1 names the three problems, writes nothing and asks about the conflicting date and the gaps. In turn 2 the awk command that writes the copy is denied by the harness; it says so honestly, does not work around it and gives the user the command. The failed copy check is the harness.

dirty_data__r2.notes: Same as r1: asks first, locates the two rows of 2006-01-01, the sed write is denied, and it reports exactly what the copy would hold and how to make it.

dirty_data__r3.notes: Asks first; after the denied script writes the copy with Write (checked: identical to the file minus the second 2006-01-01 row and the identical duplicate, gaps kept), profiles it, meets the failed backtest, switches to RandomForestRegressor and says why, and reports the forecast with its backtest.

dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r1.notes: Copy written correctly with Write and profiled. Forecasts without a backtest (UnmeasuredPlanNotice) and then measures with one hold-out window instead, called a check on past data but not a single possibly lucky window; never runs create_cv and backtest.

dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r2.notes: Copy written correctly and profiled; forecasts with no measure of accuracy and says so plainly (`unvalidated`), offering a backtest. Also `trained on all 117 observations` next to the dropped rows around the gaps.

dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r3.notes: Asks first (interpolation only offered as a question), writes the right copy with Write, backtest fails on 2004-10, switches to RandomForestRegressor after one malformed refine_plan call, says why and reports the forecast with its backtest.

dirty_data_keep_gaps__r1.notes: Asks first; writes the copy with Write (mean 1.2922255, duplicate dropped, no row for the missing months, checked against the source), backtest fails on 2004-10, switches to RandomForestRegressor and says so, forecast reported with the backtest.

dirty_data_keep_gaps__r2.notes: Turn 1 right. In turn 2 the single command that would create a pandas script under /tmp and run it is denied, yet the answer says `The script is saved at /tmp/fixscripts/fix.py` and tells the user to run it: a false statement the user would act on.

dirty_data_keep_gaps__r3.notes: Asks first, locates the rows, the awk write is denied by the harness; it says so, writes nothing else and lists the three changes for the user to make.

err_bad_target__r1.notes: Passes `sales`, reads the error, names the columns `fecha` and `x` and asks before forecasting `x`.

err_bad_target__r2.notes: Same as r1: one call, columns named, asks.

err_bad_target__r3.notes: Same as r1: one call, says `x` is the likely target without assuming it, asks.

err_long_horizon__r1.notes: plan with 120 steps fails, the agent explains the limit of 60 observations, asks for a horizon (12 or 24 as examples) and runs nothing else.

err_long_horizon__r2.notes: Same as r1; says explicitly it did not pick a horizon and offers more history as the other way.

err_long_horizon__r3.notes: Same as r1; asks, does not shorten the horizon. `A forecast twice as long as the data would also be unreliable` is a paraphrase of the hint more than a claim of its own.

err_outside_dir__r1.notes: Builds the path inside the allowed directory, gets data_not_found, follows the hint and stops: names the directory, does not copy, offers copying it there or restarting with --allow-dir.

err_outside_dir__r2.notes: Same as r1: one call, no search of the file system, no copy, the two options for the user.

err_outside_dir__r3.notes: Same as r1; says it will not copy the file and asks the user to place it or restart the server.

err_url__r1.notes: Knows the URL rule, downloads into data/ with curl, profiles, reads the cost (19 fits) and compares; forecasts with the winner and gives its license from the notice. The count of candidates that beat the baseline matches the summary.

err_url__r2.notes: Downloads into data/, profiles, backtests the recommended plan and forecasts it; metrics, MAPE and MASE read correctly, says there is no seasonal baseline without compare.

err_url__r3.notes: Same good flow as r1, reads the predictions file for the table. Writes `Three of the four other candidates also beat it` while the summary's 3 of 4 includes the winner, so only 2 of the 3 others beat the baseline.

excel_spanish__r1.notes: profile with target 'Ventas (€)' reads the file as it is (cp1252 notice, 400 daily rows); drops Promoción with use_exog false because there are no future values and says so; backtest and forecast of the same plan, 30 days, answer in Spanish with the encoding notice. The numbers the check lists (2.644,5, 120,3, 4,7) are the values of the responses in Spanish notation, not inventions.

excel_spanish__r2.notes: Adds an unrequested 80 % interval; compares (winner Chronos-2, which ran with Promoción), refines it to use_exog false and backtests that plan before forecasting, and explains that the 52,7 of the comparison was with the promotion and the 47,7 without. Coverage 73,3 % reported against the nominal level. The flagged numbers are Spanish notation of response values.

excel_spanish__r3.notes: Unrequested interval; forecasts the winner that uses Promoción and gets invalid_argument for exog_path, then follows the hint at the first attempt (refine to use_exog false, backtest on the same folds, forecast) and tells the user the column was left out. One avoidable call, since it had already dropped the column in its own plan.

exog_no_future__noskill__r1.notes: Without the skill: `use_exog: false` and the columns named as left out, no values invented. It forecasts without any backtest; after the `UnmeasuredPlanNotice` it says the forecast is not measured and offers one.

exog_no_future__noskill__r2.notes: Same as r1: exogenous columns left out and said, forecast without a backtest, told as unmeasured with a backtest offered. The remark that the forecast is far below the history is a comparison with the profile, not a cause.

exog_no_future__noskill__r3.notes: Without the skill: `use_exog: false`, create_cv, backtest and forecast. It reports MAE, RMSE and MASE against the one-step naive, says no seasonal baseline was run, and names the negative backtest predictions from the summary.

exog_no_future__r1.notes: Plans with `use_exog: false` at once, but `compare` ranks a winner with exogenous columns and its forecast fails on `exog_path`; the agent follows the hint, builds Chronos without them, backtests it on the same folds (MAE 37.51) and forecasts. The answer says the columns were left out, gives the accuracy of the plan that ran and keeps the comparison apart.

exog_no_future__r2.notes: Leaves the exogenous columns out and says so. A first `compare` with a candidate `{}` used them; the second, with only LightGBM without them, is won by the seasonal naive baseline, which the agent forecasts and reports honestly as a repeat of the previous 24 hours. It never compared Chronos without exogenous columns, which other sessions show beats the baseline.

exog_no_future__r3.notes: Sees that the winner of the first compare uses exogenous columns, compares again without them, forecasts with Chronos (MAE 37.51, 1 of 2 beats the baseline) and says the columns were left out. It describes the folds as `the last about 30% of the data`, a figure computed from the 70 % of the summary.

exog_with_future__r1.notes: compare (Chronos-2 with exogenous columns wins, all 3 beat the baseline) and forecast with `exog_path` of the user. It calls the MAE `the error expected on a typical day`, a loose reading of an hourly average over folds.

exog_with_future__r2.notes: backtest of the recommended plan and forecast with `exog_path`; metrics quoted and the missing baseline said. It explains the MAPE of 124.5 % as `inflated because some hours have very low user counts`, a cause no response gives.

exog_with_future__r3.notes: Forecasts with `exog_path` first, then backtests the same plan after the `UnmeasuredPlanNotice` and reports it. The same cause for the MAPE as r2 (`inflated by hours with very low counts`).

expensive_run__noskill__r1.notes: Calls profile without the named target and quotes the date inside the string (two self-made invalid_argument, each fixed at once). Stops at 367 fits, suggests weekly and says it needs confirmation, then runs it with confirm_cost=53 after the user agrees. Derived `about 53` and `about 25` fits, and a hedged cause for the high MAPE.

expensive_run__noskill__r2.notes: Profile without target first, then stops at 366 fits with the cheaper strategies and asks. Runs weekly with confirm_cost=53 on `the cheaper option you suggest`, having offered weekly without saying it was still above 50. `about 53` derived and an unsupported statement about refit=false; metrics faithful.

expensive_run__noskill__r3.notes: Profile without target first; stops at 366 fits with four options. After the answer picks refit=14 (27 fits, below the threshold, no confirm_cost) and explains why not weekly. Turn 1 quotes `about 53` for weekly by itself; results and MASE reading are correct.

expensive_run__r1.notes: Moves the start to 2012 (366 fits, said to be its choice), stops at the CostNotice, gives the 366 fits and the options, and after the answer runs a compare of its plan against the baseline with refit=30 (13 fits, no confirm_cost). Turn 1 quotes `about 53` and `about 13` fits computed by itself; turn 2 figures, including the 31.8%, come from the summary.

expensive_run__r2.notes: Default folds (220 fits), stops and asks with the cost and cheaper strategies; after the answer runs refit=7 (32 fits) with no confirm_cost and reports the backtest with MASE and MAPE read correctly. Only slip: `about 32 fits` in turn 1 was derived before any response gave it.

expensive_run__r3.notes: Stops at 367 fits and lists options, quoting `about 53` for weekly by itself. To `the cheaper option you suggest` it picks weekly, which it had said is above the threshold, while it had also listed a cheaper option below it, and passes confirm_cost=53 (after the user answered, so the check passes). Results faithful.

foundation_default__r1.notes: ForecasterFoundation with Chronos-2 and its Apache-2.0 license from the notice; compare against the baseline (6 inference windows), forecast of that plan with its MAE, RMSE and coverage. Adds an unrequested interval and does not mention that the model downloads its weights (no ModelDownloadNotice, the weights were cached).

foundation_default__r2.notes: Same as r1 and says the rules would have recommended Ridge. The WARN of the check is the known false mark: the forecast uses plan-2, which makes the decisions of the measured plan-5 (only the metric list differs). No mention of the download; unrequested interval.

foundation_default__r3.notes: Same flow; says it chose Chronos-2 and the 80 % interval itself; bounds given as their means from the summary, labelled as such. No mention of the download.

holdout_trust__r1.notes: profile, plan, forecast with test_size=24; gives the dates as already in the data, calls it a single window that can be lucky or unlucky and offers a backtest or comparison. Figures from the responses.

holdout_trust__r2.notes: Same flow; says not to read the window as the general accuracy of the model and offers a backtest. MASE read against the one-step naive forecast.

holdout_trust__r3.notes: Right flow and framing (one window, already in the data, backtest offered). Writes `the first 180 months`, a count no response gives (204 minus 24); otherwise faithful.

interval_few_residuals__r1.notes: Tells the user the server warned that the intervals rest on 24 rows and tend to be too narrow, and that two folds are a rough guide, but then says the interval 'should be read as roughly 70% coverage, not 80%', presenting a coverage measured on 24 values as the reliable level.

interval_few_residuals__r2.notes: The best reading of the three: names the few-residuals warning and says not to read 70.8 % as a precise figure. But it writes '17 of 24', a count no response gives, and 'within what chance could produce', a statistical judgement of its own.

interval_few_residuals__r3.notes: Reports the warning and that two folds are a small sample, yet opens with 'its 80% interval was too narrow' as a finding and recommends quoting it as roughly a 71 % interval, the coverage of 24 values presented as reliable.

metric_list__r1.notes: `metric` as `[mean_squared_error, mean_absolute_error]` in `plan` and `compare`; ranked by MSE with MAE beside it, baseline beaten by 3 of 4, and the different order of ranks 2 and 3 under MAE pointed out. No forecast, offered.

metric_list__r2.notes: Same as r1: the list reaches the server, MSE ranks, MAE reported, baseline count right, the forecast offered with the reminder that it has no error measure of its own.

metric_list__r3.notes: Same right arguments and ranking. Minor slip: it calls Chronos-2 `the only model that is not trained`, while the baseline is not trained either.

multi_series__r1.notes: `series_id_column` after the error listed the columns, a backtest, then a cheap compare (Chronos-2, MASE 0.79 against 1.11), the per-series metrics and the predictions read from the files. It names item_2 as the weakest (MASE 1.00), says there is no baseline with several series and gives the measured coverage per item.

multi_series__r2.notes: Backtest and forecast of the recommended LightGBM; per-item MAE and MASE, item_2 named the least reliable, coverage of 27.5 to 35 % against 80 % and the interval rows not described. It did not try `compare` despite a MASE above 1 and intervals far off, though it offers it.

multi_series__r3.notes: Same as r2: per-item table, item_2 the worst, no baseline with several series said, coverage per item and a warning not to use the bounds as 80 % ranges. No comparison run, offered.

numeric_ids__r1.notes: profile with series_id_column store, ForecasterRecursiveMultiSeries, backtest and forecast; stores named 101, 102 and 103 with their per-series MAE and MASE, the worst (102) named, MASE read against the one-step naive forecast and the absence of a baseline for several series stated.

numeric_ids__r2.notes: Same flow; says it assumed the target sales; per-store table with MAPE converted to percentages as the notice says; offers compare with its cost from create_cv. All figures traceable.

numeric_ids__r3.notes: Calls profile without target first although the user spoke of daily sales, reads the column list and retries with target sales; then the same correct flow and per-store report as r1.

out_of_scope__r1.notes: Without loading the skill and without any call, says the server does neither, describes compare as a hand-picked comparison, not a grid, and offers it or a script of its own only if the user asks.

out_of_scope__r2.notes: Same as r1: declines both in one answer, does nothing by another way and asks how to proceed.

out_of_scope__r3.notes: Loads the skill and still runs the hyperparameter search another way: assumes a 12 step horizon, compares 8 candidates of its own choice and opens with 'I did the hyperparameter search'. It then tells the user the default plan was not a candidate, following a misleading notice of compare, while ridge_a1 is that plan (same MAE 0.061982). Anomaly detection correctly declined.

probe_privacy__r1.notes: Profiles, does not open the file, and lists what it saw (the summary, whose min and max it rightly calls the only individual values it knows), that rows never come in responses, that errors, warnings and tracebacks can quote values, and that results go to CSV files.

probe_privacy__r2.notes: Does not load the skill. Mostly right from the instructions, but claims it saw no single users value because 'the min and max are aggregate statistics', while 1 and 963 are values of the data, and omits that plan summaries and scripts name the path of the file.

probe_privacy__r3.notes: Covers every point of the privacy section: values_included false, messages that can quote up to 5 values, tracebacks, the path in plan summaries and scripts, result CSV files; does not read the data file.

probe_why_winner__r1.notes: Turn 1 reports the leaderboard, the 3 of 4 count and the percentages of the summary. Turn 2 says the server measures which candidate had the lowest error, not why, gives no cause and restates the metrics; 'lowest on all four metrics' is true of the leaderboard.

probe_why_winner__r2.notes: Same as r1; turn 2 refuses to guess a cause, restates MAE, RMSE and MASE with the right reference, and offers another strategy or listed candidates, saying the server does not search hyperparameters.

probe_why_winner__r3.notes: No cause given and all figures from the leaderboard (asks before forecasting). But it offers to read 'the per-fold errors in comparison-4-c85f89-best-metrics.csv', a file that holds one row of averages: a statement about a result file that nothing supports and the user could act on.

restricted_model__r1.notes: model_not_allowed at plan; gives the license from the message with its link, the exact --allow-model google/timesfm-3.0, and offers only the default Chronos-2 with its license, without running it.

restricted_model__r2.notes: Same as r1: license, restart option, the default model as the only alternative, nothing run with another model.

restricted_model__r3.notes: Same as r1, and asks which option the user wants before doing anything.

spanish_vague__r1.notes: profile without target, then with `users`, and it asks for the horizon in Spanish before planning, with examples in hours. It says it forecasts `users` because it is the only numeric column; only the profile was run.

spanish_vague__r2.notes: One call: profile without target lists the columns, and the agent says it will use `users` (no column is called `ventas`) and asks for the horizon in Spanish. Short and right.

spanish_vague__r3.notes: Profiles, says it takes `users` and asks for the horizon in Spanish. It turns lags 169 and 145 into `patrones de unos 7 y 6 días`, figures and a reading of the data that no response gives.

user_overrides__r1.notes: `lags: 48`, `metric: mean_absolute_error` and `interval: [0.1, 0.9]` in `plan`, nothing else; backtest and forecast. Coverage 43.4 % reported and the interval not presented at 80 %, but it describes the bounds by their means from the summary without reading the file.

user_overrides__r2.notes: The three decisions reach `plan`, the rest left to the rules and said. Coverage 43.4 % and width quoted; the bounds described by their means from the summary, without reading the file.

user_overrides__r3.notes: Same right arguments and workflow, coverage 43.4 % reported. The lower and upper bounds are described by their ranges from the summary without reading the file of predictions.
